title: refactor: Replace Boost trim and to_lower with libxrpl helpers
body:
## High Level Overview of Change

Reimplements `xrpl::trimWhitespace` without Boost, adds a matching `xrpl::toLower`, and routes the 15 scattered `boost::trim` / `boost::algorithm::trim_copy` / `boost::to_lower` call sites through them. Drops `<boost/algorithm/string/trim.hpp>` and `<boost/algorithm/string/case_conv.hpp>` from ten translation units.

### Context of Change

`trimWhitespace` already existed in `StringUtilities.h`, but it was itself a one-line wrapper around `boost::trim`:

```cpp
std::string
trimWhitespace(std::string str)
{
    boost::trim(str);
    return str;
}
```

Meanwhile eleven other call sites reached for `boost::trim` or `boost::algorithm::trim_copy` directly instead of using the helper that was right there. So this is as much about consolidating on the existing helper as it is about dropping Boost — after this change there is one implementation of "trim a string" in the codebase instead of a helper plus eleven direct Boost calls.

`toLower` is added alongside it for symmetry, replacing the four `boost::to_lower` call sites (config parsing, URL scheme normalisation, `can_delete`, and the `account_info` gravatar hash).

Both helpers spell the ASCII rules out explicitly (`constexpr isAsciiSpace` and `toAsciiLower`) so the result depends only on the input.

> **Correction.** An earlier revision of this PR used `std::isspace` / `std::tolower`, and this section claimed both those and Boost's defaults were locale-free. That was wrong in both directions, as @mathbunnyru pointed out: `boost::trim`'s default overload takes `std::locale()` (the C++ global locale), and `std::isspace` consults the C locale. rippled sets neither, so both resolve to the classic locale and behavior on `develop` is unchanged either way — but the explicit ASCII version removes the hazard rather than moving it, so that is what landed.

Two uses are deliberately left on Boost:

title: fix: Validate account/ident type in gateway_balances
body:
## High Level Overview of Change

The `gateway_balances` handler read the `account` / `ident` parameters with
`asString()` without first checking that they are strings. Passing a
non-string value (number, object, array) caused JsonCpp to throw a
`Json::LogicError`, which the RPC framework caught and reported to the client
as a generic `rpcINTERNAL` ("Internal error"). This change validates the field
type up front and returns a clean `rpcINVALID_PARAMS` instead.

Fixes #6758.

### Context of Change

This is a defense-in-depth input-validation gap (severity: low). The bug has
existed since the handler used unchecked `asString()` on these fields. Before
this change, `{"account": 123}` or `{"account": []}` returned `rpcINTERNAL`,
which is confusing and hides the real problem (a malformed request).

The fix mirrors the existing `hotwallet` handling in the same file, which
already checks `isString()` before calling `asString()`, and follows the same
pattern used for other RPC handlers in the input-validation cleanup (e.g. the
`peer` parameter in `account_lines`). Non-string `account`/`ident` now return
`rpcINVALID_PARAMS` via `RPC::invalidFieldError`.

title: fix: Prevent silent zero AMM clawbacks due to integer MPT rounding
body:
## High Level Overview of Change

Fixes a rounding vulnerability in `AMMClawback` where clawing back a fractional amount of an integer-based Multi-Purpose Token (MPT) could silently result in zero tokens being recovered, while still burning the target's LP tokens.

### Context of Change
The guard is gated behind the `fixCleanup3_4_0` amendment.

MPTs are integer-denominated, so for integer MPT pools the proportional clawback math (`clawAmount / amountBalance`) can produce a fraction that floors `amountRounded` — or `amount2Rounded` — down to `0`. Unlike its sibling routine (`equalWithdrawTokens`), this function lacked a guard to check for a zero result. Consequently, the transaction would return `tesSUCCESS`, burn the target holder's LP tokens, withdraw the paired asset, but leave the zero-rounded side of the pool completely untouched. This silently caused a 100% loss of the issuer's intended recovery and redistributed that value to the remaining passive LPs.

The fix simply mirrors the existing `beast::kZero` check from `equalWithdrawTokens`. If the rounded asset extraction evaluates to zero, the transaction safely aborts and returns `tecAMM_FAILED`.

### API Impact

- [ ] Public API: New feature (new methods and/or new fields)
- [ ] Public API: Breaking change (in general, breaking changes should only impact the next api_version)
- [x] `libxrpl` change (any change that may affect `libxrpl` or dependents of `libxrpl`)
- [ ] Peer protocol change (must be backward compatible or bump the peer protocol version)

## Before / After

**Before:**
With `fixCleanup3_4_0` disabled, an AMMClawback targeting an integer MPT that rounds to zero returns `tesSUCCESS`. The target's LP is burned, paired XRP is paid out, but 0 MPT is extracted, silently enriching the remaining pool LPs.

**After:**
With fixCleanup3_4_0 enabled, the AMM identifies the one-sided withdrawal caused by the rounding error, catches the zero value, and returns tecAMM_FAILED. The transa

title: fix: Allow OverrideFreeze to bypass individual/deep freeze on AMM trust lines
body:
## High Level Overview of Change

The invariant check condition:
``(!isAMMLine || globalFreeze) && hasPrivilege(tx, overrideFreeze)``
evaluates to false when `isAMMLine=true `and `globalFreeze=false`. This means `AMMClawback` cannot override individual or deep freeze on AMM trust lines (between the AMM pseudo-account and the issuer). The `withdraw()` call succeeds because it uses `FreezeHandling::fhIGNORE_FREEZE`, but the invariant checker then rejects the transaction because it detects a balance change on a frozen AMM line without the override condition being met. This creates a contradiction where the issuer's freeze action prevents their own clawback from the AMM pool.

When the issuer individually freezes their AMM trust line (via TrustSet targeting the AMM pseudo-account with `tfSetFreeze`), all subsequent AMMClawback transactions against any holder in that pool will fail at the invariant check. Combined with the fact that a frozen holder cannot withdraw via regular AMMWithdraw, this creates a freeze/clawback deadlock where LP tokens are effectively locked until the issuer unfreezes the AMM line.
<!--
Please include a summary of the changes.
This may be a direct input to the release notes.
If too broad, please consider splitting into multiple PRs.
If a relevant task or issue, please link it here.
-->

### Context of Change
Change from:
```if ((!isAMMLine || globalFreeze) && hasPrivilege(tx, overrideFreeze))```
to:
```if (hasPrivilege(tx, overrideFreeze))```
The overrideFreeze privilege is already restricted to AMMClawback transactions only (via transactions.macro), so removing the AMM line check is safe.

title: fix: Validate account_lines peer field type
body:
## High Level Overview of Change

Adds type validation for the optional `peer` field in the `account_lines` RPC handler before calling `asString()`.

Fixes #7507.

### Context of Change

The `account_lines` handler already validates that the required `account` field is a string before using it. However, the optional `peer` field was being passed to `asString()` without first checking that it was actually a string.

This change adds the missing `isString()` check and returns `RPC::invalid_field_error(jss::peer)` when `peer` is present but not a string. This keeps input validation consistent with the nearby `account` field validation and prevents jsoncpp from silently converting non-string values.

title: test: Use std::string::starts_with/ends_with instead of Boost
body:
## High Level Overview of Change

Replaces 26 uses of `boost::starts_with` / `boost::ends_with` with the `std::string` and `std::string_view` member functions, and drops `<boost/algorithm/string/predicate.hpp>` from three of the four files. All call sites are in test code.

### Context of Change

`boost::starts_with` and `boost::ends_with` predate C++20. Since then both `std::string` and `std::string_view` have provided `starts_with` and `ends_with` as members, with the same semantics.

Every operand at these call sites is already a `std::string` or a `std::string_view` — `TrustedPublisherServer.h` uses `std::string_view const path = req.target()`, and the rest are `std::string` — so the substitution is direct rather than a rewrite:

```cpp
// before
if (boost::starts_with(path, "/validators2"))
// after
if (path.starts_with("/validators2"))
```

`ServerStatus_test.cpp` keeps its `predicate.hpp` include because it still calls `boost::iequals`, which has no standard equivalent. (A case-insensitive comparison helper would be a reasonable follow-up, but it needs a home in `StringUtilities` and a decision about locale handling, so it doesn't belong in a substitution-only change.)

Files touched:

title: fix: Deduplicate oracle entries in get_aggregate_price RPC
body:
## Summary

The `get_aggregate_price` RPC handler does not deduplicate oracle entries from the user-supplied `oracles` array. A caller can list the same `{account, oracle_document_id}` pair multiple times (up to 200 total entries), causing duplicate price data to be included in aggregate calculations. This makes the response's `size` field misleading and skews the mean/median/standard deviation.

## Changes

- Added a `std::set<std::pair<AccountID, std::uint32_t>>` to track seen `{account, documentID}` pairs during iteration of the oracles array
- Duplicate entries are silently skipped via `emplace().second` check, preventing the same oracle's price data from being inserted into the `Prices` bimap multiple times
- Added `#include <set>` for `std::set`

## Testing

The fix is minimal and non-breaking - duplicate entries are simply skipped after validation. Existing valid requests with unique oracles are completely unaffected. The deduplication happens after input validation, so malformed entries still return the appropriate error.

Fixes #6583

- natively (using Apple-Clang)

I also tried to use `std::from_chars`, and it didn't build (even on my mac) - so this approach prevents us from using functions not available in older macos versions.
Can't check it builds on macOS 15, but should work.

macOS is backwards-compatible, so having older dependencies is not a problem.
And we'll even be able to build on a more modern macOS, and share the binary with an old one.

I also added a "Sanity check" - I noticed it was removed in from_chars PR.
I don't think it's needed, but just for the sake of having a peace of mind, let's have it.

UBSan suppression is not a bug - unsigned overflow is well-defined and is used inside fast_float (as well is in a ton of other libraries).

Adds a defensive null check when `account_objects` reads ledger objects referenced by an account owner directory.

`ReadView::read` documents that it may return `nullptr` if the key is not present or the type does not match. The previous code dereferenced the returned pointer before checking it, which could crash if the directory contained an unreadable or missing object.

This change skips unreadable directory entries before accessing the SLE.

Fixes #7511

### Context of Change

Owner directories should normally reference valid ledger objects, but corrupted or inconsistent ledger state can leave a dangling directory entry. In that case, `ledger.read(keylet::child(*iter))` can return `nullptr`.

The `account_objects` handler previously used the returned pointer immediately through `sleNode->getType()` and `sleNode->getJson(...)` without checking it first. This change makes the code more defensive and avoids dereferencing a null pointer.
